title: Serial enrichment incubation technique (SEIT) for rapid isolation of plant growth-promoting bacteria: Saving researcher time and lab resources
author: Maheshwari, Parmar, et al.
materials: Isolation of calcium-dissolving bacteria (CDBs) from plant samples.

steps.title: Prepare selective enrichment broths
steps.instruction: Prepare the following liquid media in 10 ml aliquots (per tube) and add nystatin at 50 µg ml⁻¹ (or 50 mg ml⁻¹ as originally stated). Adjust pH as indicated and add the specified insoluble nutrient source and pH‑indicator dye:

substeps.instruction: Iron‑free succinate broth (for siderophore producers): K₂HPO₄ 6.0 g L⁻¹, KH₂PO₄ 3.0 g L⁻¹, MgSO₄·7H₂O 0.2 g L⁻¹, (NH₄)₂SO₄ 1.0 g L⁻¹, sodium succinate 4.0 g L⁻¹, pH 7.00.

NBRIP broth (phosphorus solubilizers): D‑glucose 10.00 g L⁻¹, Ca₃(PO₄)₂ 5.00 g L⁻¹, MgCl₂·6H₂O 5.0 g L⁻¹, MgSO₄·7H₂O 0.25 g L⁻¹, KCl 0.2 g L⁻¹, (NH₂)₂SO₄ 0.10 g L⁻¹, pH 7.0, bromophenol blue 0.01 g L⁻¹.

Calcium‑differentiating broth (calcium solubilizers): Glucose 5.00 g L⁻¹, Yeast extract 1.00 g L⁻¹, Peptone 1.00 g L⁻¹, K₂HPO₄ 0.4 g L⁻¹, MgSO₄·7H₂O 0.01 g L⁻¹, NaCl 5.00 g L⁻¹, (NH₄)₂SO₄ 0.05 g L⁻¹, CaCO₃ 5.00 g L⁻¹, bromothymol blue 0.01 g L⁻¹.
Aleksandrov broth (potassium solubilizers): Dextrose 5.00 g L⁻¹, MgSO₄·7H₂O 0.50 g L⁻¹, FeCl₃ 0.005 g L⁻¹, CaCO₃ 0.10 g L⁻¹, Ca₃(PO₄)₂ 2.00 g L⁻¹, KAlSi₃O₈ 2.00 g L⁻¹, bromothymol blue 0.01 g L⁻¹.
Zinc‑solubilizing broth: Dextrose 10.00 g L⁻¹, (NH₄)₂SO₄ 1.00 g L⁻¹, KCl 0.20 g L⁻¹, K₂HPO₄ 0.10 g L⁻¹, MgSO₄·7H₂O 0.10 g L⁻¹, ZnCO₃ 1.00 g L⁻¹, bromothymol blue 0.01 g L⁻¹.

General enrichment broth (used for the first description): 10 ml of any of the above media adjusted to pH 8.00, containing an insoluble source of the target nutrient (tricalcium phosphate, CaCO₃ or Ca₃(PO₄)₂, mica or KAlSi₃O₈, ZnCO₃) and the three indicator dyes (bromophenol blue, bromothymol blue, bromocresol purple).

steps.title: Inoculate samples into broth
steps.instruction: For each sample, add either 0.1 g of crushed solid plant/soil material or 0.1 ml of liquid sample (for the general enrichment) – or 1 g (solid) or 1 ml (liquid) when using the specific nutrient broths – into a 10 ml tube containing the appropriate broth prepared in Step 1.

steps.title: Incubate enrichment tubes
steps.instruction: Seal the tubes and incubate them for 5 days at 28 ± 2 °C (or 30 ± 2 °C for later plate incubations).

steps.title: Serial transfer to fresh broth
steps.instruction: Aseptically transfer 100 µl of the suspension from each tube showing any colour change into a fresh 10 ml tube of the same broth. Repeat this transfer twice more (total of three successive 5‑day incubations) until the tube discolours (yellow for phosphate/calcium, orange for siderophore, yellow from blue/green for potassium or zinc).

steps.title: Serial dilution of final enrichment
steps.instruction: From the final (third) enrichment tube, prepare a dilution series: 10⁻¹, 10⁻² and 10⁻³ in sterile saline or buffer.

steps.title: Prepare selective agar plates
steps.instruction: For each nutrient type, prepare agar medium by adding 18 g L⁻¹ agar‑agar to the corresponding broth composition (including the same pH indicator dye and nystatin at 50 µg ml⁻¹). Autoclave the broth and the agar separately, then mix the hot agar with the sterile broth under a laminar flow hood and pour into sterile Petri dishes.

substeps.instruction: CAS‑nutrient agar for siderophore screening: Prepare 100 ml CAS dye solution (60.5 mg CAS in 50 ml water + 10 ml 2 mM FeCl₃·6H₂O in 10 mM HCl + 72.9 mg HDTMA in 40 ml water) and combine with 900 ml nutrient agar; autoclave separately and mix before pouring.
NBRIP agar (phosphate), calcium‑differentiating agar, Aleksandrov agar (potassium) and zinc agar are made by adding 18 g L⁻¹ agar to the respective broth recipes listed in Step 1.

steps.title: Plate diluted suspensions
steps.instruction: Spread 100 µl of the 10⁻³ dilution uniformly onto the corresponding agar plate. Invert the plates and incubate for 5 days at 30 ± 2 °C. Keep the plates for an additional 24 hours to allow colour development.

steps.title: Identify positive colonies
steps.instruction: Examine plates for the expected colour change and/or clearing zones: • CAS plates – blue to orange (siderophore). • NBRIP plates – yellow (phosphate). • Calcium plates – yellow (calcium). • Aleksandrov or zinc plates – yellow from blue/green (potassium or zinc). Retain only plates showing a stable colour change and a clear zone around colonies.

steps.title: Purify isolates
steps.instruction: Pick each positive colony and streak onto nutrient agar (no selective agents) to obtain pure cultures. Incubate the streaked plates under the same temperature conditions until isolated colonies are visible.

steps.title: Record and store isolates
steps.instruction: Label each purified isolate, note the sample origin, the nutrient type it solubilised, and the time to colour change (early change indicates higher acid production). Preserve cultures by glycerol‑stocking at –80 °C for future work.
